Params: What does the cosmic noise sound like? Physicists, communications experts, and literary scholars all give different answers.
Perhaps because the last thing you felt was the ocean, what reaches you now is its chorus.
It rings inside and out, wandering through time and space, singing of the richness and ruin of civilization, wild as a storm, never staying.
Ahead of you, Ananke's streams of light float softly, like anemones sheltering small fish, like strands of fate still loose on the loom.
To get back to the right time when I was sent here...
I have to find the moment Ananke reaches peak operation, the exact moment the Atlantic Calamity breaks out.
You let yourself be carried by a tide that has no substance, drawing near to the threads of light, reaching toward the reality that shows through their gaps.
Talk. How did you get in here? The family armory requires five levels of clearance. It's impossible to get through without all of them.
Will we... see each other again?
The part you found is me... and the part you haven't... is also me?
You know we can't actually touch.
You see countless versions of Adelyde. In the places those countless Adelydes cannot see, you say goodbye.

The edges of your vision are etched with the imprint of every light stream you have touched, and your sense of self solidifies out of the void. The world around you dims, while a single point of light in the distance grows brighter and brighter.
Light and sea twist into a whirlpool, surging toward that one point.
The search is still ongoing. We can't let our guard down.
When Gray Raven commits to a mission, we see it through.
...The sea's so big, and you're crossing it by yourself?
Everyone waiting for you, in the past, the present, and the future, and the calamity that struck twice. All of it lies on the other side.
(Should I hold my breath before jumping in?)
Against every instinct for survival, you dive into the deepest part of the whirlpool.
Ma'am, we've lost contact with the rest of the formation. Every frequency's jammed, and it's bad!
Keep trying. Report back the second you get through!
She barks an order at the subordinate behind her, then snaps her attention back to you, her guard still fully raised.
The moment you realized you could take physical form, you had already taken care to put on a protective mask.
Where the hell did this person come from? Whose job was it to screen the passengers?!
Ma'am, we ran a full biometric scan after boarding. There was no intruder—
Gray Raven is my informant and confidant, with info logged into the family database by me years ago. Gray Raven was waiting at your last port to rescue me.
Adelyde's breathing has steadied. She glances your way, a silent reassurance in her expression.
Then she stands from the seat, pulls the pilot, now awake, out from behind the chair, and presses a firm hand to the nape of his neck.
Steer clear of that blue surge.
Behind you, the cabin rises into noise as passengers wake, their groans and startled cries tangling with the soldiers' shouted orders.
Alyssa's brow stays furrowed. She clearly does not believe Adelyde's explanation, but she keeps her voice low, pitched so only those nearby can hear.
Our mission came through the family's most classified channel. Your clearance was revoked years ago. There's no way you could've known ahead of time, let alone set any of this up!
You think so? Go ahead and convince yourself however you want later. Right now, we've got bigger problems.
Adelyde casts a sharp look at Alyssa, then points at the towering surge beyond the window.
If you don't know, then tell me everything unusual you can remember.
I'm not your enemy, Alyssa. We both want the same thing right now: to get to the Atlantic Eye and see Rusalka. Without answers, we're just circling up here.
The woman in the family soldier uniform sweeps a dark look between you and Adelyde, then gives a curt, reluctant nod.
I got the mission straight from Lady Rusalka herself. A few days ago, I made a quick run to the Atlantic Eye.

The only thing off was some lab coats in the elevator talking about a big project about to wrap up. Something the head of the Erhorn family was personally invested in, set to be announced after the Day of Enlightenment ceremony.
The analysis of the "Understanding" Sefirah is complete.
Unlike before, when your words went unheard no matter how hard you tried, this time they reach Adelyde clearly.
Yeah. I tried telling you plenty of times before. Never worked.
"Only what's already happened is free from the laws of time, and only that can be spoken"... What you said is true.
Information you have held back for so long finally breaks loose, and your thoughts race.
Adelyde, do you know what a Sefirah is? And the Consciousness Tide?
Adelyde's mouth presses into a thin line, and she nods.

The last course Dominik taught before leaving the Atlantic Eye was on this. He said a Sefirah is a node interface through which humans extract information from the Consciousness Tide. But why would the development of that interface...
Information can be converted into energy.
And at the scale of the collective unconscious, the energy it converts into is beyond imagination.
You're saying this surge is Consciousness Tide energy?
Correct. Think back. When it struck you, what did you feel?
It was like... dissolving into an ocean of human consciousnesses.
All color drains from the face of the young woman before you.
Arius detonated the human collective unconscious. If we can't seal that surge... can our individual consciousness even continue to exist?
No one can answer that. In the suffocating silence that follows, a status report and an incoming comm request ring out from behind you at the same moment.
The signal intelligence system is back online. Top-priority comm request from the Helio family head, asking for... for Miss Adelyde Helio!
But the family head hasn't been active for years. Lady Rusalka has been handling things in his place.
A hoarse voice crackles from the terminal, and yet every family member and employee in the cabin straightens up to listen.
Adelyde. I know you're on the transport headed for the Atlantic Eye. You saw the explosion with your own eyes.
The last message we received before comms went dark reported catastrophic losses among personnel and assets inside.

Effective immediately, all your defiance of family decisions and reputational damage will not be held against you. I'm appointing you Commander of the Atlantic Eye recovery operation. All resources in Sector EOA-01 are yours to command.

You have only one mission: get there before the World Government and the other Transatlantic families, and recover as many critical tech assets from the dam as possible. This operation is strictly confidential.
Strictly confidential? Sir, with our family's resources alone, our salvage capacity will be severely limited. I don't understand—
Because it's not only about how much we recover; it's about how much we can't let them pull out!
The man sputters between ragged coughs, gasping for air, yet every word he speaks is iron.

I don't have time to explain the disastrous power reshuffling that will follow. This deal has failed completely, and we Helios will never allow them to use relief efforts to carve up the fruits of our labor.
Take what you can carry. If you can't take the equipment, take the data. If you can't save the people, save the backed-up memories from their chips.
If the operation succeeds, I will hold a press conference immediately and announce you as the next head of the family.
One last question: while we lead the team into the Atlantic Eye, will the family be sending additional personnel to the affected residential islands nearby?
Before he can finish, Adelyde cuts the line. She sways, bows her head, and presses a hand against the Helio crest on her chest.
The sharp metal edges bite into her palm. Blood winds downward, running over the bright sun and onto the blue gem, like a line of cloudy tears.
At some point, the cockpit door and the cabin door have both been pulled open, and a flood of voices—cries, whispers, and panic—crashes over her.
My... my sister just got to Gardener Island yesterday. What the hell does the family head mean by that?
What about the people who don't have backed-up memories?
Damn it! Pick up, come on! Aren't the comms back?!
My family's served the Helios for three generations, Commander. Save us first—
The crowd surges toward her, hands reaching for the hem of Adelyde's clothes. The family soldiers who can still lift a gun no longer know where to look, so they use their bodies as a wall.
(Help the family soldiers keep order and keep the people off Adelyde)
Adelyde. You're the only one who can give orders right now.
The moment Adelyde sees you standing between her and the crowd, taking the shoves meant for her, something in her eyes jolts.
"You need to know what you're fighting for."
"You need to know what you're fighting for."
She bites hard on her tongue. The taste of blood clears her head, and she lifts her voice.
Anyone with family on the nearby residential islands, raise your hand.
The cries die out. In the quiet that follows, a single sob escapes someone in the crowd. Hands lift, shaking, full of hope and dread and a desperate need to hear more.
Alyssa's eyes are wet and rimmed red. She lifts her hand, jaw locked. Adelyde looks straight at her, unflinching.

Alyssa, you're leading the rescue team to the residential islands. Once the others are delivered to the dam below, I'll allocate half of our transports and vessels to you, including crew, technicians, and supplies.
Don't let down the people who believed in you most.
She shouts several names, calling people out to organize into squads. She turns to go, then stops mid-step. She spins back, presses a fist to her chest.
It's the salute shared between F.O.S. students.
Adelyde returns the gesture with quiet solemnity. Neither of the two former schoolmates says another word.

Use every channel available through the signal intelligence system, including the private ones on my terminal, and broadcast a humanitarian distress call across the globe in the name of the Transatlantic Economic Community.
State plainly that the Atlantic Eye suffered a catastrophic explosion due to a major internal experimental accident. And transmit the exact coordinates of all available entry points.
Open a public rescue ops channel. Sync everything across it. Supplies, equipment, and intel from the Helio rescue team are shared through the channel.
Those are the orders of the operation commander.
Adelyde slams her fist against the bulkhead, then lifts her head to meet the eyes fixed on her.
Just now, the family that raised me, that I would have given everything for, betrayed everything it stood for.
"Think broadly" doesn't mean choosing selfishness when unity is what's needed most.
"Take initiative" doesn't mean planning an escape route when a solution is what's needed most.
"Stay true" doesn't mean talking about profit when faith is what's needed most.
The white-haired woman's voice comes out ragged, but her eyes grow brighter with each word.
As if a white-hot fire burned in her soul, reckless and absolute, she digs out a handful and holds it before everyone like a spark.
I am the heir of the Helio family, a Watcher of the Atlantic, the champion of F.O.S. I am also a daughter, a student, a teacher—
And someone just like you, scared when staring down a disaster that none of us understand.
I'm afraid of being abandoned. Afraid that the people I hold dear are somewhere below us, buried in the ruins at the bottom of the sea. Afraid that I'll throw my life away for nothing.
But I still have the strength to fight back. I still have a chance to save the people I care about. And I still have this life to give everything I've got!
Maybe all of this will end in blood and sweat, with everyone turning their backs on us and no miracles left to speak of. But that day is not today.
Even if no one follows, I'll break through the abyss and charge straight into hell. And if all I can do is steal a boat from the Styx and ferry people back, then that's what I'll do.
This is my belief. And now, I need yours.
The words hit the cabin like a strike.
Outside, the ocean continues to heave, and the disaster continues to loom. The plane is a leaf in the dark, tossed between sky and sea, and still, inside it, a calm silence spreads.
A female researcher drops into her seat and opens her terminal, fingers flying, head down, while her colleagues stare in stunned silence.
Got no last words to write? If you do, hurry up.
She throws Adelyde a single look, then nudges her glasses higher on her nose.
I like your guts. I'm going down with you.
Me too! I'm done working for those armchair generals. From now on, I'm with you!
Tsk. Real classical. Does someone have ancient Greek speeches for dinner?
What really moves people is power straight from the heart. Well said, Ade.
Before the signaler, the public channel panel, until now a field of black, lights up with two glowing points of access.
The transmissions are from F.O.S. College and the Spelmin family.
This is Instructor Arakna of F.O.S. Military Command College. The College knows what's going on. We're calling up instructors and senior cadets right now.
Heading out now. See you at the Atlantic Eye.
This is Helentine of the Spelmin family. Our family is rerouting nearby ships for rescue and evacuation. Once I've handled the situation on Jareit Island, I'll lead a team there myself.
Hold in there, everyone. You won't be fighting this alone.
More lights blink on, one after another, like a sea of stars igniting across the night sky. Voices follow close behind, rising and falling, arriving from distant places.
This is the World Government Emergency Management Division.
This is the Deep-Sea Operations Division of the Cosmos Technicians Union.
This is the North Atlantic Liaison Center of the Arctic Route Union.

People begin taking over the comms on their own. Amid the hiss of static and electric current, Adelyde buries her face in her hands, shoulders trembling. Her voice comes out so soft it barely reaches the air.
Thank you. Thank you, all of you.
Her thumb quickly wipes the dampness from the corner of her eye. Then the operation commander lifts her head with grim resolve.
We're going to bring everyone up from below, alive.
And drag Arius up here and get some answers.
